channel.title: nexusEVnews
channel.description: Independent EV and renewable energy news, curated daily. Electric vehicles, solar, battery tech, and charging infrastructure.

item.title: Porsche's Quickest Cayenne Ever, and the Case for Buying the Cheap One
item.dc:creator: carwow
item.description: Carwow times the Cayenne Electric Turbo at 2.46 seconds to 60 mph and 9.98 over the quarter mile, then argues the entry level car is the one worth buying.

item.title: Denza's 1,604 HP Supercar Has Four Seats and a Fridge
item.dc:creator: Electrifying
item.description: Three motors, 1,604 horsepower and a cool box that runs to minus six. Electrifying drives the Z at Goodwood and confirms UK pricing from just under 143,000 pounds.

item.title: A 108 kWh Cayenne Nearly Out-Ranged a 140 kWh Rivian
item.dc:creator: Out of Spec Reviews
item.description: Out of Spec ran both cars to a stop at 70 mph. The Cayenne managed 344.7 miles on 108 kWh, against roughly 356 miles from a Rivian carrying about 30 kWh more.

item.title: The Silverado EV Max Range Adds 323 Miles in 46 Minutes
item.dc:creator: Gjeebs
item.description: A 205 kWh battery, a 478 mile rating and a $95,000 as tested price. Gjeebs charged it from 10 to 80 percent in 46 minutes and recommends the trim below it.

item.title: The Subaru Uncharted Nails the Drive and Misses on Efficiency
item.dc:creator: CarSauce
item.description: All wheel drive, 5.02 seconds to 100 km/h and one of the best rides in the class. CarSauce could not better 20.3 kWh per 100 km, and that changes the maths.

item.title: The bZ Woodland Is Toyota's First EV Worth Cross-Shopping
item.dc:creator: Doug DeMuro
item.description: Doug DeMuro reports around $47,000, 375 horsepower and 280 miles of range on a wagon shaped electric SUV developed with Subaru and sold there as the Trail Seeker.

item.title: The Denza Z Drifts and Parks Itself, at a Fraction of Hypercar Money
item.dc:creator: Supercar Blondie
item.description: Three motors and just over 1,600 horsepower, priced at roughly 150,000 to 200,000 euros. The party trick is a car that drifts and parks itself while nobody is inside.

item.title: A NEVI Site Actually Opened, and Two EV Drivers Built It
item.dc:creator: State Of Charge
item.description: State of Charge visits PowerUp America's first site in rural Kentucky: a canopy, pull through stalls, tap to pay and both connectors on all four ports.

item.title: Replacing an Ioniq 5 Drive Motor Means Dropping the Whole Subframe
item.dc:creator: Out of Spec Renew
item.description: A 153,000 mile Ioniq 5 with an intermittent shutdown, an $8,000 dealer quote, and a used drive unit fitted instead. Two brackets are all that stand between this job and a simple one.

item.title: Waymo's Safety Numbers Look Great. Comparing Them Is the Hard Part.
item.dc:creator: InsideEVs
item.description: An IIHS study puts Waymo in 68 percent fewer crashes than human drivers. The InsideEVs podcast digs into why that comparison is much harder to make than it sounds.

item.title: Lexus Built an Electric ES That Behaves Like the Gas One
item.dc:creator: Auto Focus
item.description: Auto Focus drove a late prototype and reports a single motor, around 220 horsepower and a rear floor tunnel that has no reason to exist in a front wheel drive electric car.

item.title: Audi Brought Back the A2 by Chasing Efficiency Instead of Battery Size
item.dc:creator: Electrifying
item.description: A camouflaged prototype driven in Sweden with a 58 kWh usable pack, 190 horsepower and a 0.24 drag coefficient. Electrifying reports 4.4 miles per kWh, with a support car managing 5.55.

item.title: Five Pounds of Fuel Against Five Pounds of Charge, on the Same Road
item.dc:creator: Andersen EV
item.description: Five pounds of petrol showed about 40 miles on the gauge. Five pounds of overnight home charging filled a Renault 5 to 100 percent and 215 indicated miles. The result rests entirely on the tariff.

item.title: A Silverado EV Range Test Run the Way Families Actually Drive
item.dc:creator: Outsider Reviews
item.description: Two adults, a child, two dogs, cargo and climate control running front and rear. The video reports 642.7 km covered with 5 percent remaining, and a gauge that disagreed with the navigation.

item.title: Australia Wants EV Drivers to Pay by the Kilometre
item.dc:creator: ABC News In-depth
item.description: From July next year, New South Wales EV drivers face a charge of almost 3 cents per kilometre. ABC 7.30 reports fuel excise raises around $15 billion a year and the base is shrinking fast.

item.title: Five Minute Charging, Sodium Home Batteries, and the Slow Road to Battery Planes
item.dc:creator: Everything Electric
item.description: Robert Llewellyn and Oxford chemist Saiful Islam on 1.5 MW flash charging, sodium ion home storage and why solid state is still five to ten years out. Recorded on stage at Latitude.

item.title: The Self-Driving Story Nobody Is Telling
item.dc:creator: Jacob Hunka
item.description: The autonomy debate is all horse race. But for millions of people who cannot drive, a car that drives itself is the keys, handed back. Why Rivian's road to Level 4 matters more than the spec sheet, and the one thing it still has to get right.

item.title: We Built the Tracker We Wish Existed When We Were Waiting for Our R1s
item.dc:creator: Jacob Hunka
item.description: People were reading website source code to find out when their Rivian was coming. Forum signatures listed Guide contact dates like military service records. We are not doing that again for the R2. The Rivian R2 Delivery Tracker is live.

item.title: Two Batteries, One Hitch, and the Case for All-Electric Glamping
item.dc:creator: Jacob Hunka
item.description: The Lightship AE1 carries its own 69 kWh battery and 80 kW motor to neutralize trailer drag on the tow vehicle. Paired with a Rivian, the real-world efficiency numbers are hard to argue with. This is what all-electric glamping looks like when the hardware actually works.

item.title: Atlanta, Rivian, and the Quiet Coincidence
item.dc:creator: Jacob Hunka
item.description: Atlanta has a failing air quality grade and a Rivian plant on its doorstep. A hypothetical about what one city could do with the electric mobility infrastructure that already exists — R2 autonomous taxis, ALSO cargo quads, e-bikes, and ZTL-style restricted zones — and what the health data says the stakes actually are. Includes data from the HEI lockdown air quality study (Chen et al., 2025) and the American Lung Association's 2025 Atlanta air quality report.
